utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. General, if I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, last time when we closed, there was the question of whether the evacuation agreement should be admitted as an exhibit, and my learned friend Mr. Vasic had some objections to that. The Prosecution has since been speaking to the Defence on this point, and Mr. Vasic has kindly agreed to contact General Raseta to actually find out from him whether or not he signed the document. And then once that is known, we propose the matter can be taken from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. We will hold things as they are for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: General, last time you were giving your evidence we had just looked at the evacuation agreement and the question of signatures. We would now like to move to another document which we would like you to comment upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: If I could kindly ask the court clerk to call up document bearing 65 ter 209, ERN ZA004342, and that is only an English translation. There is not a B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: General, do you have a copy of this document?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, this is a document in English which is being read to you in the Croatian language which is essentially an order from General Tus to the commands of the various ZNG units operating in Vinkovci and Osijek, concerning there to be a cease-fire in that region on the 20th November to allow the convoy to go through. Now, are you aware of that document, since it was copied to you?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of this document. This is the usual way to pass orders down to the relevant units on the ground, cease-fire orders specifically. If I may make one observation in this English translation, I think there is a mistake. It says the 11th of November, whereas it should most probably read, actually I'm quite certain, the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I ask this document to be exhibited with the permission of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be exhibit number 94, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Could I ask the court clerk to please call up document bearing 65 ter 210, bearing ERN 00099955. And B/C/S, 03269948.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Are you able to see this document, General?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am now.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And this is a document which I believe you have sent to General Raseta concerning the evacuation of the hospital on the 20th of November and that the evacuation route should be secured. Is that a correct assessment of this document?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. This is a proposal I made following a previous oral agreement with General Raseta. You can see that this is not the same route that had been agreed on the 18th of November. This is an alternative route being proposed here, crossing JNA-controlled territory and going on into Bosnia and to the lower or southern river-bank of the Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I ask that this document be exhibited, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be exhibit number 95, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'd like to turn to another document which is in fact the reply to your proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And if I may kindly ask the court clerk to call up document 65 ter 209 bearing ERN ZA004343. Unfortunately, this document is only in English. There is not a B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: General, do you have a copy of this document?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it on my screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: In essence, this document is dated 21st of November, 1991 and it's actually from General Raseta agreeing to your proposal. To your recollection would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we please -- yes, yes. That's the one I mean. Yes. This is indeed his reply, as far as I can remember. I saw it and acted accordingly, in accordance with my letter dated the 20th of November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I ask the Court that this document be exhibited?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On behalf of the Defence teams, I would move that this document be marked for identification for the time being, for the following reasons. On the face of the document we see nothing but the English translation. We have never received a B/C/S copy of this document. And based on all the documents that we have so far seen, the documents based on letters written by Mr. Raseta that we have not objected to, we realise that originals were used. I don't believe this is an original document. If the OTP does indeed have a copy in B/C/S, a signed one needless to say, in that case we would not challenge the document. However, as there appears to be an English translation of the original bearing no signature, we would propose that this document be marked for identification and then we can pursue this subject further with Mr. Raseta and verify the authenticity of this document. We do not believe that this can be considered an authentic document given that this is only an English translation and there appears to be no original, at least none that's been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be number 96, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just to clarify on the point of translation, it had been the policy of the OTP that where a document had been submitted in a previous case, as was in this case, Milosevic, and there was no translation, generally as a rule we did not pursue a translation, but now if this is the case we will pursue such a document and produce it for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. The important issue for admission is the original or a satisfactory best copy available of the original. This clearly is not an original or a copy of it. It's an English translation at best.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And this is what we are try and sort out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'd like to turn to another document now, which was actually written on the 26th of November, 1991, after the evacuation of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: If I can ask the court clerk to kindly turn up on the E-Court 65 ter 211, bearing translation in the English -- one moment while I find the ERN. 00269903. And B/C/S, 03269903. I beg your pardon, actually with the English, it's 03269903. The copy was blurred that I was reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have that number but not in English, Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: If you would bear with me, the English is ET 03269903.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Same number, both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: General, do you have a copy of this document?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And this is a document by Dr. Mate Granic, written to the honourable ambassador, Ambassador D.J. van Houten, the chief of the ECMM, mentioning about the JNA occupational forces getting even with civilians and prisoners and release of Mr. Bili Vidic. Now, firstly, could you tell the Court who Dr. Mate Granic is?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Mate Granic was assistant prime minister in the Croatian government, the government gave him the task of monitoring the negotiations and quite generally relations with the ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And are you aware of this correspondence?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I ever received this letter myself, but I do know that Dr. Mate Granic wrote to Ambassador van Houten about this. We were in touch almost permanently at the time. I do believe that this is an authentic signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I request the Chamber that this document be exhibited?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be exhibit number 97, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, General, once again, after the evacuation of the hospital, the question arose as to where some of the patients had gone. So with the court clerk's assistance, I would like to call up document marked 65 ter 212, with English translation 03269880, and B/C/S translation 03269880. And I should make clear the B/C/S is actually the original, and it's the English which is the translation. General, do you have this document on your screen?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And this is a letter from Professor Andrija Hebrang to the European mission concerning the destiny of the wounded from the hospital staff, and it is essentially saying that according to the list only a small number of the hospital staff was received contrary to the agreement and contrary to the Geneva Conventions. So even at this date, 27th November, it is apparent that there are missing patients from the hospital staff. Are you aware that Professor Hebrang wrote such a letter?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of the fact that he had written this letter. He interceded on several occasions. This is just one of many letters that were sent to the European mission dealing with this or similar problems. Professor Hebrang, Croatian health minister, was charged with dealing with the hospital evacuation and negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And do you know whether any satisfactory response was ever received about the whereabouts of the patients pursuant to this letter by Dr. Hebrang?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we received this letter, the same day or the next day, it was placed on the agenda of our bilateral meeting, the meeting between General Raseta and myself. I remember that his answer at the time was as follows: "You will be receiving a reply in due time. For the time being we can provide no further details other than what you already know." There was a worrying answer about the fate of the prisoners who did not arrive in that convoy that was received in Sremska Mitrovica, and we never received another response from Raseta.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Can I ask the Court, please, to exhibit this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be exhibit number 98, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn to another letter which again is from Professor Hebrang of the same date, 27th of November. This, however, doesn't concern the hospital convoy and its evacuation. Rather, it concerns the difficulties being faced by the Croatian community in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the court clerk to kindly call up the this document. It's under the same 65 ter number as the last document and has B/C/S number 03269881 and English translation 03269881.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, do you have this document before you?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And in essence, this document concerns the need to evacuate various people from Lovas. Can you comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lovas is a village that had been putting up resistance against the aggression for quite a long time. It was surrounded by JNA units and what were most probably paramilitary units too. Once it had been taken, there was immediately information on the situation of these citizens who were inside the half-occupied and surrounded village. I'm not sure how the information reached us, by which route. Professor Hebrang then appealed to the European mission to make a plan for evacuating these people. We can see here that he's proposing several evacuation routes. It was his belief at the time and my proposal that Hungary might be one of the possible routes where the evacuation would be quickest and easiest, and there is a proposal for evacuation by helicopters and an alternative was to use the River Danube. None of these proposed routes were accepted by the JNA. They had the village under control and there was nothing the Croatian side could do about it. We learned later on that the people captured at Lovas had been forced to stray into minefields, as a result of which many were killed and some were again captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Can I ask that this document be tendered as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be exhibit number 99, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, General, as you can see from the last document, which we addressed we are now moving away from the evacuation of the hospital and the expulsions of Croatian citizens from other parts of Croatia by the JNA in league with paramilitary forces. So the next document I would like to call up bears 65 ter 213, and has translation of 00310190. And we only have an English copy because actually it's an information that has been received following a meeting with Prime Minister Granic on 15th of January, 1992. Now, you'll see at paragraph 1, this is actually a meeting which you attended. And at paragraph 4, the two Croatian priorities were to halt the process of intimidation of Croatians out of their homes in areas under JNA control, as well as to halt their replacement by Serbian settlers and to secure an early withdrawal from the JNA. You also see on paragraph 5, which if I can ask the court clerk to turn the next page of the document, is that minister Budisa claimed that Serbia was using the truce to achieve its war aims primarily the forcible ejection of Croatians from occupied territory and the systematic settlement of Serbians in their place. Now, you also mention at paragraph 12 that in certain territory, which was 98 per cent Croatian, no excuse could be advanced for the JNA to enter to protect minorities. Now, do you recall this meeting?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I remember that we had this meeting at the Hotel I, I believe, Hotel I. That was about a fortnight before Spain took over Presidency of the European mission. It was Ambassador Salgueiro who took over in 1992. I think this was one of the first meetings that were held. This was also 12 days after the Sarajevo truce on the 2nd of January, 1992. The UN occupation troops tried to reinforce and fortify the lines reached that were already under their control. A large number of complaints were received from those areas, caused by the actions of the occupying forces. This faithfully reflects the situation in the occupied areas and the general mood during this particular round of negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I ask the Court that this document kindly be tendered as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be exhibit number 100, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, again, General, on the point of Croatian populations being expelled from villages in hand with the JNA and Serbian paramilitaries, I'd like to call up another document, which is 65 ter 214, with English translation, ZA002090, and B/C/S, ZA002091. Now essentially this is a fax which you received about the expulsion of Croatians from a Croatian village of Boksic by Chetniks right under the very noses of the JNA and you requested the urgent sending of the ECMM team to look into the situation. Now, can you tell us who Iljo Kobas is, the person who sent the document?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document in front of me. As for the gentleman, the teacher who signed this document, Professor, as he signed it, I don't know this person but it's quite obvious that this is the secretary for Zuljpanja [phoen] municipality because that's what the stamp indicates. It is quite obvious that information had reached him on the displaced persons, displaced residents of the village of Boksic, which is obviously again next to the village of Cakovci because that's where he states the Chetniks had entered Boksic from. You can see the handwritten comment at the bottom of the page, this is something that I wrote, and addressed to Mr. Ramljak, the vice-president of the Croatian government. I wanted this to be shown to the Croatian news agency and the Croatian state TV. I also asked that the ECMM from Belgrade be sent over in order to protect the citizens on their way out.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And did the ECMM monitors go there to that village and protect the civilians, so far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that. An ECMM group that was based in Belgrade eventually went there, and I don't remember what sort of information I received later.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned in your handwritten note that you believe there will be an escalation in the displacement of persons. Did your prophecy prove correct? Did it escalate the displacement of Croatian persons?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the truce was established on the 2nd -- or rather, 3rd of January, 1992 the occupation forces started cleansing the remaining parts of the Croatian territory that they had taken. The scale was more massive in some areas and the process was a little slower in other areas. Certain people managed to linger on in the areas for quite a long time. I don't know how they managed. The concern expressed in the last sentence proved to be fully justified at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, General, who do you actually mean by the occupational forces?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean those who were in control of that particular territory. I'm talking about Eastern Slavonia and all the way to the confrontation line. In my submission, the JNA units were responsible. They were supposed to have control or had effective control over all the units that were controlling the area. A popular name for those where I come from used to be Chetnik units, or alternatively TO units that got involved right at the beginning when the whole thing started in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I ask the Court that this document be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be exhibit number 101, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, we have been discussing the expulsion of the Croatian population and I now come to a document dated 28th of March, 1992, which is again on this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: If I could ask the court clerk to call up this document, 65 ter 215, with ERN 00796553, and we only have an English of it. There is no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, this document is from General Nambiar, the UNPROFOR in Sarajevo, to Goulding of the United Nations in New York, and it concerns a meeting attended by Mr. Ramljak and yourself as well as others, and it's addressing the expulsion of the Croatian population, in particular in the villages of Tovarnik and Nijemci. Now, you also, on page 2 of this document -- and if I can ask the court clerk to move to page 2, in the second paragraph, it says that Mr. Ramljak spoke in strong terms about daily reports of plundering, expulsions, coercions, especially in the three regions mentioned, and that you, Agotic, in the fifth paragraph, stress the importance of the technical coordination under joint auspices of UN and ECMM. Now, do you recall such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that we did have a meeting. I think it was in -- on the -- at the premises of the Croatian assembly and that was perhaps the first meeting with General Satish Nambiar, the European -- the Croatian parliament. It was attended by those people who are mentioned here, and besides the Croatian side, members of the ECMM were also present. Ambassador Salgueiro was mentioned here, the Chairman at the time. That was when we talked about the tasks that needed to be carried out in relation to the territories under occupation. The task was supposed to be carried out by UNPROFOR. I don't know English well enough in order to be able to follow the text and to confirm whether it's reported the way it was. But I know that I was present at that meeting and that I did attend subsequently a series of meetings of similar content.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I ask the court that this document be exhibited?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 102, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, general I know that you're aware of General Anton Tus and some of the activities of the ZNG due to opposition. And I'd like to turn to a document which has already been marked for identification as number 71, and it's 65 ter 184, with English ERN RO320966. And it's a newspaper article entitled "the war was won by blockading the garrisons," and it's based on a lecture given by General Anton Tus, the chief military adviser to the president of Croatia. Now, in essence, General, in this document, General Tus, amongst other matters, points out that one of the tactics of the ZNG was to blockade the JNA barracks with a view to acquiring weapons because the Croatian armed forces had hardly any weapons, having been disarmed. Would that be a correct policy?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know General Tus well. We worked together, and up until the end of 1992, he was the chief of the Main Staff of the Croatian army. Then he became military adviser to the president of the republic. I cannot really guarantee because I don't know English well enough in order to be able to read the document, so I don't know what its contents are exactly, but I know that in his lectures he would always give an assessment such as this one and that I actually agree with that. Whether he assessed the development with the barracks situation in such a way that it was necessary to obtain weapons for the ZNG or to be able to take weapons from the JNA for the paramilitary, perhaps that was something that could have been discussed, but this was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, also during the same lecture and in the same document, General Tus mentioned that the aggressor gave up on the occupation of all of Croatia and attempted to at least achieve the goals set forth in the memorandum and to capture parts of Croatia to the Karlobag-Karlovac-Virovitica line and that is why the large battle was for Eastern Slavonia and its cities, Vinkovci, Osijek and Vukovar. Now, does General Tus's assessment in his lecture fall in line with your evidence that there were three plans: Plan A, the taking over of the whole of Croatia; Plan B, up to the Karlobag-Karlovac-Virovitica line; and then finally the truncated Plan C which was largely the cities in Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But Plan B was to reach the Virovitica-Karlovac-Karlobag line and to capture the Croatia area there, including Bosnia, all the way or all the areas that were east of that line. When they realised that it was not realistically possible achieve this plan, then they embarked on the implementation of the so-called Plan C, achieving control over 30 per cent of the territory of the Republic of Croatia, which was actually realised by the end of 1992, and it was sanctioned with the cease-fire in Sarajevo on the 2nd of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I ask the Chamber that this document previously marked as number 71 be exhibited?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, General, as we have been running through various documents, we've touched upon numerous areas and towns and cities in Croatia. And I think it would be of assistance to the Chamber if perhaps we could look at the location of some of these towns and cities on a map so that it's easier for the Chamber to familiarise itself. So I'd ask the court clerk to kindly call up map 4, which is 04626620. Can you indicate when the map is appearing, General?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: And if I might ask the Court for assistance in providing the general with a marker, because, General, I'd like you to mark or circle various of the locations which you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the map now. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Before I ask the general to proceed with the marking, may I submit to the Chamber that we exhibit this map as a blank document and then thereafter give a new exhibit number to the document which he marks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 103, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, general, this is a map which shows a part of Croatia and has many of the towns and villages which you've mentioned in your evidence. So could you kindly circle on the map Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Ilok.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Lovas.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll find it in a minute. You can't really see all that well. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Tovarnik.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Nijemci.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Roughly where the Bruska village is?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bruska.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Bruska.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bruska, the village of Bruska is near Benkovac. It's on another part of the map. It's in western Croatia, near the Adriatic coast, near Ravni Kotari.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: We will look at a second map in a moment and perhaps we can do those markings on those maps. Now, in your evidence, you mentioned the Virovitica-Karlobag-Karlovac line, the so-called Plan B line. Could you kindly draw for us where that line is on this map, if it's possible?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not possible on this map. It's -- it shows only the eastern part of the country, while this line is more to the west from -- in relation to this part. All I can mark here is the eastern sector, which was occupied. I can mark that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Yes. If you could mark the eastern sector line, please, and then we'll mark the other line on another map.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. East of this line was the occupied territory of the Republic of Croatia, later named sector east, once the UNPROFOR forces arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: May I kindly ask that this map be exhibited, saved as, with the markings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 104, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, can I ask the court clerk to kindly call up another map? And this is map number 3, bearing ERN 04626619.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, General, you were a member of the security services for about 20 years, and you've explained in your evidence in the Milosevic case, which has also been admitted into evidence in this case how the chains of command of the security organs and other ordinary reporting lines were in the JNA. So my question to you is: If a commander of a unit gave a security officer a particular order, for example, the evacuation of a hospital, would the security officer need to report on the progress of the implementation of that order to the commander who gave him that order?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes. He would have to do so. Each order by the commander had to be carried out by any member of the unit. If the security organ received an order from the commander, then he was obliged to inform his line of management of the service, along -- according to his competency, and then they would have to begin implementing it. Then all the tasks that were implemented had to be reported on. If he received the order from his commander, he would report to the commander, as well as to his line of command of the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: That completes the 92 bis (B) procedure for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Agha. Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General. I would like to introduce myself first. I am Mr. Vasic, and I am Defence counsel for Mr. Mrksic. Because we both understand and we speak the same language, I would like to ask you to pause after my questions so that the interpreters would be able to interpret our dialogue into English so that others who don't speak our language would know what we are saying. Hopefully there won't be any problems because you have already testified before at this Tribunal. For a moment I would like to go back to your military career so that we would know what jobs you performed at certain time periods, which would be relevant to the questions that I will be asking you. Your career in the JNA began in 1966 in Pula, and then in 1968 you already became the commander of the reconnaissance centre of an air force unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My military career started after I completed the military academy on the 27th of September, 1965. The -- I became a commander of a radar station or unit in Bihac in the course of 1968 or in early 1969.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Three years after this, you became chief of security of the 117th Combat Fighter Regiment?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a combat air force fighter regiment, and I have been a chief of security or the chief of security since 1974.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: General, and when do you -- when did you become the deputy chief of the military security department of the 5th Air Force Corps in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became deputy -- it wasn't an official title, but I was the assistant of the chief in 1974. This was in June of 1974.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The 5th Corps was subordinated to the air force command in Zemun, was it not?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: After you completed the war college in 1986 you became chief of security of the 5th Air Force Corps?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Several months after I graduated, I became chief of the security services of the 5th Air Force Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You remained in that position until March 1991, when you were removed from your post by your superior, Slobodan Rakocevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: My apologies. In July 1991, you requested and received approval to quit the military service?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: As early as at the beginning of August, you became Chief of Staff of the National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When the Main Staff of the Croatian army was established in September 1991, you became commander of the air force and anti-aircraft defence?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander of the air force and anti-air force defence, I became commander of the air force and anti-air force defence in early September 1991 -- in early December 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In 1996, did you receive a promotion to the rank of Lieutenant Colonel and were you appointed deputy Chief of Staff of the Main Staff of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. In 1996, I was awarded the rank of Colonel General, but I was named assistant Chief of Staff of the Main Staff of the Croatian army for the air force and anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It was in December 2002 that you retired and your rank at the time was staff general, which would have been equivalent to the rank of army general in the former JNA, would it not?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true. My rank was staff general. That is equivalent to a four-star general. But there was another general level rank in wartime in the Croatian army. It would be very difficult to translate into a different system but it would have been the equivalent of an army general in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was that the top-most rank that could be achieved in your army?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would have been the highest rank with the exception of those who were in the position of chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: After your retirement you became adviser to the president of the republic, first for defence and military-related matters, and following that, adviser for national security?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became adviser to the president of the Republic of Croatia even before I retired, when the Croatian president, Stipe Mesic, began his first term of office. After I retired, I became adviser for national security and remained in that position until the end of his first term of office.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When I look at your impressive military career, we must agree that for over 20 years you were involved in security-related tasks and matters. When you were a JNA officer, you were in a security unit of the air force that covered the whole territory of the former JNA. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. There is one thing that is debatable, whether it covered the entire territory of the former Yugoslavia. From a professional point of view, that can be debated but I believe more questions will follow about that later, so let's not waste time on it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In addition to all the military schools that you completed, in addition to your practical experience in the army, you also obtained an MA degree from Zagreb's political sciences faculty?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was back in 1985.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: While you were an active officer, the air force structure broke down into corps, did it not?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was after the last reorganising scheme, and up to that point, it had been different, and many different systems prevailed throughout my career.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: After this new corps level organisation, the first was in Nis, the third was in Zagreb, and the 5th was in Zagreb, and you were chief at the time; right? In each and every one of these, there were security departments that were subordinated to the chief of the war air force in Zemun; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And chief of security of the air force was subordinated to the chief of the security administration of the secretariat for All People's Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Which territory was covered by the 5th Corps of the -- 5th Air Force Corps which you were part of at the time?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 5th Air Force Corps covered the area to the east of the following line: Virovitica-Banja Luka-Split, or rather to the west of the line that I just described.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So we can conclude that they covered the entire territory of Slovenia and southwest Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The north, the northwest, and the west of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were talking about your tasks in your statement, and in your testimony that has been tendered into evidence here, the transcript, about the tasks that the security administration of the federal secretariat for All People's Defence handed out to their subordinated security organs. These tasks subdivided into roughly three groups, neutralising the actions of foreign intelligence services, neutralising the activities of extremists from the immigration circles, and countering the domestic or internal enemy?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, globally speaking. But another thing was protection of confidentiality which was also essential to what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: At the relevant period of time, just before the events of 1991, unlike the air force, the land forces were subdivided into three military districts; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which three those were and which territories they covered?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Military District in Belgrade, the 3rd Military District in Nis, and the 5th Military District in Zagreb. As for their respective territories, I can't say with certainty, but they did not overlap with the territory covered by the air force, although to a very high extent they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. What about the 5th Military District based in Zagreb? Was it not made up of 5th -- five corps?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were five corps. I've listed them all in my statement in a previous trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Rijeka, Zagreb, Ljubljana, Maribor and Varazdin?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Each military district of the land forces had security departments headed by chiefs, as well as counter-intelligence groups, did it not?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we had security sections not departments - it's a slightly higher level - and counter-intelligence groups, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What was in the course in the air force was at the military district level in the land forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the air force, at the air force command level, there was the central or rather counter-intelligence group which had three detachments in the respective corps headquarters. But these were not subordinated to the corps. They were subordinated directly to the central intelligence group of the air force command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this a convenient time, Mr. Vasic? We will have the first break now and resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: General, during the break the interpreters asked me to slow down a little and to pause between our questions and answers. On the 29th and 30th of May and until the 1st of July 2002, did you give a statement to the OTP? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I gave a statement but I don't remember the exact dates. That must be indicated on the statement, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the different units of the air force, and specifically those of the 5th Air Force Corps, you said that the 5th Corps had several air force bases and that each had a security organ?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You also said that each of the bases had a military police unit subordinated to the security department?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that was as far as professional matters were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And the same applied to the land forces?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In your statement you described two parallel chains of command that applied to security bodies. For military matters, the chain went all the way up to the commander of the air force, and in the land forces, the commander of the military district. The other chain, as far as professional matters were concerned, went to the chief of security administration of All People's Defence, and this applied to both the air force and the land forces?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly speaking that's true, except that this part went up only as far as the corps. Whichever command had a security body, this security body was subordinated to the commander, first and foremost, as far as military matters were concerned. As far as purely professional matters were concerned, technical matters, we didn't call it a chain of command. We called it a chain of control.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the activities of security bodies? Was not most of their work about technical aspects?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The -- these technical aspects mostly depended on the chief of the security organ. Can you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The more the security organ dealt with technical and security issues, the more successful it was because their superior for technical issues always insisted that they deal, as much as possible, with technical aspects, which did not imply that they would not have followed the orders of their commanders where military matters were concerned. There had to be some sort of a balance, however, between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the importance of security organs or bodies in the JNA? It was great, wasn't it, in relation to those officers who were not part of the security chain, as it were? Were security bodies consulted when officers were appointed to command positions?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: If their opinion was negative, could it have resulted in someone not being appointed?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were cases like that, but there were cases where the security organs opposed somebody's appointment and this person was still appointed. Then there would be appeals to the superior command structure at a higher level. These appeals sometimes failed. But in most cases, where the security organ had some authority, in their work with the commander, they would normally be successful in imposing their position and their opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Let us now consider the period of late 1990 and early 1991. What about the activities of the security administration in this period? You said that it became a command structure and that security channels were used to pass on the most important orders in the JNA in this period of time. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to say, to define the time line from when until when, but yes it's important that -- it's true that important information was passed down that chain, and most of the instructions that were received from positions higher up were based on information collected by the service, not necessarily all but the best part.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigators of the OTP, did you not say that the federal secretary, Kadijevic himself, at the time, believed the security channel to be the most reliable and the fastest way at the time to pass information and orders up and down the command chain in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true. But that statement was in reference to the beginning of the war in Croatia. I'm not sure about Slovenia. That was in reference to that time. I wasn't talking about 1990 and 1991 in their entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So this would be in reference to the second half of 1991, if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that would be an accurate way of putting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When you testified in a different case before this Tribunal, did you not say about this that the then-chief of the security administration, Aca Vasiljevic, could have passed information down the security channel without informing the relevant commanders?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. Whether he informed anyone about that or not is not for me to say. Whether he informed his own superior, the federal secretary for All People's Defence. However, within the service, information was being passed on that I think the superiors in the chain of command were not necessarily familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the independence enjoyed by security officers when dealing with technical issues pursuant to orders from their own superior security officer and in relation to their own unit?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where technical matters were concerned, they would have been entirely independent. However, from the rank of army commander or military district commander later on, and higher up the chain, those officers would have known everything that their security organ was doing. Down the chain there was selective information being passed around, such information as concerned technical issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the security organ would have been in a position to use certain activities concerning these technical aspects without informing their commander?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does this position of the security organ indicate the existence of a separate chain or special chain of command in relation to orders and in relation to higher or superior organs of structure?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does indicate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: At the time that we are speaking about, was a security officer authorised to hand over a JNA member or a civilian suspected of committing a crime in relation to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that security officer did not have that right. The only right that he had was in an emergency situation was to detain a person if there were grounds to suspect that person, and they could hold the person until the investigative organs arrived on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: We talked about activities of the security administration and the security organs in neutralising certain factors or certain destabilisation factors of the social order. The third of those activities was to neutralise internal enemies. At a certain period in time, did this third activity become a priority activity, as far as the security organs were concerned?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It did become a priority.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Countering the activities of internal enemies, did that refer to internal enemies of all the nations and nationalities that lived in the SFRY at the time?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: After 1976 [as interpreted], this segment of activity of the security organs was given a special form in uncovering members of the so-called irredentist movement. These were internal enemies of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say that it was from 1986. I would say that it was from an even earlier time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was the culmination -- an event that occurred in a barracks of the JNA at the time, did that event draw special attention of the organs of security to this problem, if you know what I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct. If you have the transcript, that is where I already explained this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Considering all of these circumstances, was there a justified concern because of this organising tendency by the irredentist forces?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a concern in that respect but I think that certain individuals exaggerated it and occasionally abused it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You said that it was exaggerated and abused by certain individuals. Could you please tell us who you mean when you say these individuals?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about Albanian nationalism specifically and the irredentist movement as we refer to it officially within the security services at the time, some individuals that were heading the service insisted that irredentist organisation had to be found in any unit of the JNA. For example, if there were any three Albanians in any given unit, they were an organised threesome. So there was a certain number of individuals within the security service who managed to impose this view on the service. So that is what I mean when I say that there was an abuse of this occurrence in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One of the people who created such an approach regarding the irredentist movement was Mr. Aca Vasiljevic. Would you say that was true?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that and I think that at the time, he and his team were one of those individuals in the 7th Military District. Excuse me, in the 7th Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And did this method of work spread throughout the service when Mr. Vasiljevic became the chief of the SSNO security administration?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It spread throughout a considerable part of the service, and those security organs that had not uncovered any irredentist activities were considered to be unsuccessful in their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you personally have a problem in regard to this matter, in terms of your relations with your superiors from the security organs?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to a certain extent, I did. I managed to resist that. And in the 5th Corps, there was not a large number of cases of irredentist, nationalist organising. There were individual cases which were considered as indicative, and my superior at the time considered that to be an unsatisfactory assessment and -- a reflection of unsatisfactory work.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: A colleague of yours from the security service, Mr. Bogdan Vujic, did he come to the -- to your corps in connection with this uncovering of irredentist occurrences in your corps?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember Mr. Vujic from that time. He was a travelling ambassador at the time throughout Yugoslavia. He travelled when these irredentist movement events were topical. He did come to the 5th Corps as well. I personally did not work together with him in his team, even though in that period we did have frequent contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: He was a specialist in uncovering irredentist cases?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He could have been considered a specialist in that area in the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And did your information lead you to believe that he was an honourable officer?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a person who had quite an imagination, and he put in a lot of effort in his work. He could work for days without a break, conducting interviews and so on. But as far as I know, he was an honourable officer and he did not set up or stage any organisations or cases in this respect in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you have information as to how he identified irredentist threesomes in the area of the 5th Corps?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that we had a very insignificant number of such cases, and I did not directly participate in these activities. This is something that my deputy did at the time, Lieutenant Colonel at the time. I don't know exactly what his role was, the role of Colonel Vujic in specific cases, but I do know that he was considered to be a person who provided considerable assistance in these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When you were testifying before this Tribunal, did you say that Mr. Bogdan Vujic, in uncovering these irredentist threesomes, requested a list of soldiers of Albanian ethnicity from a unit and would then proceed to declare them as members of the irredentist movement?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A list of members of the unit would be a starting point in order to make assessments aimed at future activities. So he probably did request such lists. He couldn't begin without that. However, I do know that he, as well as the other individuals who worked on uncovering these threesomes, would make setups on paper of their organisation and then would proceed to acknowledge or would proceed to gain confessions from these individuals, that they were a member of these threesomes without enough elements that would justify such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that they were practically forcing them to admit that they were members of such cells?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As well as by having established some sort of cooperation with them, and enter into certain arrangements. However, when such cases would come to trial, they would not usually be successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And was this work that was done by him valued within the framework of the security administration?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes. I wasn't at the security administration, but there, at that level, it was a help to the people who were working on these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Is it your opinion that Colonel Vujic did this because it was particularly valued in the service or he did it because he had something against soldiers of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that he had anything against any soldier of any nationality, but that was a trend at the time. He agreed with such a policy and such a trend, and he took part in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And did he cooperate with Mr. Aleksandar Vasiljevic in this trend?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he probably did report to him but I don't know what their relationship was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you say that in this period, after these activities were implemented against internal enemies, members of the irredentist movement, that he actually surrounded himself with his own people who shared his beliefs?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, who shared his beliefs, but who also blindly followed him and obeyed him. Yes, he did surround himself with such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was Bogdan Vujic a member of that team?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogdan Vujic, I think, was about to retire at that time. I don't know whether he had an important post or not in the security administration at the time, but he did enjoy the rank of colonel, the reputation of a senior, experienced person. So this is something that he brought with him. However, I really don't know what his relations were with Aca Vasiljevic, but I assume that they were close.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: During the 1980s, during this phase of neutralising internal enemies, and at the end of the 1980s, when different political parties were created in the territory of the SFRY, did the focus of the security organs shift from internal enemies so that now the service began to look for associates among the ranks of these new political parties?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The Communist Party or the League of Communists of Yugoslavia was the ideological basis within the JNA, were there any attempts at the time in order to create a new such basis through the League of Communists Movement for Yugoslavia, and if such a thing did occur, who was the architect of such an idea and such a policy?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct. There were attempts to create the League of Communists Movement for Yugoslavia. As far as I know, initiators were certain retired generals and admirals of the JNA, specifically Mamula, Mirkovic. They were generals. And they included in those activities persons from other republican centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was this in fact an attempt to preserve cohesion in the army and to prevent the break-up of the country?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's what they believed. I think that was the intention that mattered, since they eventually opted for this platform. Objectively speaking, even now, and it has been 14 or 15 years since, we see that their attempt or their effort was groundless. Personally, I did not agree with their platform and I wished no part in it. That was one of the reasons I clashed with my superiors in the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Were Mr. Vasiljevic and Mr. Rakocevic, whom we mentioned today, part of this endeavour?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic and Mr. Rakocevic were -- it's difficult to be specific about the time, but I think it was back in 1988 and 1989, they were a priori in favour of preserving Yugoslavia, and I can say that I was too. It was in this sense that they opposed every form of nationalism. As time went by, and the multi-party system was allowed and subsequently introduced, they looked for a party throughout Yugoslavia that was strong enough and powerful enough to be able to implement their ideas. They found a candidate in the Socialist Party of Serbia, more specifically in the person of their party president. It was at this point in time that they left behind Serb nationalism, which, like any other nationalism, would eventually have destroyed Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In the late 1980s and early 1990s, did we not have a situation where certain high-ranking JNA officers were being monitored by the security forces as suspected of being Serb nationalists?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the case. But, like I said, that was up until 1989, perhaps even 1990. But back in 1988 or 1989, I'm convinced, because I myself attended a number of such meetings and lectures, where the two of them, on behalf of the security administration, branded or condemned all forms of nationalism.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: After the multi-party elections that we briefly touched on, and following the victories of national parties in some of the republics, did the military leadership not at that point believe that there was a real danger that the leaderships of Croatia and Slovenia would use force in order to cause the breakdown of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Assessments like that were voiced among the JNA leaders at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the result of these assessments and decisions that were made by the chief of the General Staff? I mean his decision to disarm the Territorial Defence units of all the republics and autonomous regions? I mean his decision to place all the weapons thus requisitioned under the control of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From where he was standing, this assessment was real, and the result of this fact was the decision that he gave. This was not only an act of usurpation on his part but he was also usurping other people's property because the TO's equipment was the property of the republics. Without thinking twice, he requisitioned all of this and placed it under his own control.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But the decision was only about placing the weapons under control. These weapons were not taken away from the republics and autonomous regions. The weapons were still, technically speaking, property of these republics?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on paper. In reality, it boiled down to who was in possession of these weapons and who had access to them. It no longer mattered who the weapons technically belonged to. The physical reality was altogether different.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to Aleksandar Vasiljevic's appointment as chief of the security administration. What is your opinion of Mr. Vasiljevic as chief? What exactly was the extent of his power in that position?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Mr. Aleksandar Vasiljevic was a very able officer, very intelligent, very versatile. He was very good at making assessments. He was very good at following through with his assessments, and he was able to impose himself on other people. I think he was very good at selecting his associates and he was very good at organising the service in order to carry out the tasks that he believed were crucial at the time, at least as far as his aspect of activity was concerned. Had he been successful, or rather had the JNA leadership managed to remain neutral in what happened in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, there would have been a monument built to honour them all now. But they took sides, the leadership of the JNA took sides, and we all know what happened as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Let's leave this topic for a moment. In relation to your last answer, according to the constitution, did the JNA not have a duty to protect the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the entire SFRY?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true. That was one of its duties. However, what was necessary at the time was to recognise the political realities. Once the multi-party system had been allowed, there was no longer any way we could influence which party would be victorious in the elections, which is something that the JNA tried to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So what's your conclusion? Was it a problem that the JNA didn't act according to the constitution or because the system was not adapted to the new realities that the country was facing after the multi-party elections?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The constitutional system was not modified to fit the new realities. For that, you needed to have a new consensus by the leaderships of all the individual republics and not for the JNA to make independent decisions as a political agent.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Let us now, please, go back to the security chief. When you spoke about Mr. Vasiljevic to the investigators of the OTP, did you say that his associates in the security administration respected him and feared him in equal measure?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the feeling I had. I had the impression that he was a very authoritarian person in the way he treated those who were around him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that they carried out his ideas and designs?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that to have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was he at the time influential even with the federal secretary, who made decisions based on Mr. Vasiljevic's opinions?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was very influential. I can't be more specific, but I know that I personally in 1989 and 1990 and in early 1991 repeatedly wrote to the federal secretary in order to inform him about the situation as it was at the time in Croatia and Slovenia. Some of the information that came from that general direction was quite contrary or different from my own assessments and information that I had obtained in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you suffer any consequences in your work on account of that, on account of these erroneous assessments?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I suffered some consequences, and this climaxed on the 2nd of March, 1991. I was removed from my post because my assessments were different from those of my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In relation to this topic, did you state to the investigators of the OTP that the decisions of Admiral Brovet who was assistant federal secretary and of Aleksandar Vasiljevic became in actual fact orders?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that based on certain decisions, I had that feeling. The same applies to the information/order of the chief of the Main Staff which we discussed yesterday, dated the 12th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that any decision by Mr. Vasiljevic would have the same effect with his subordinates as if it had been made by the military leadership itself?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think it carried quite the same clout, because it would not have had the same consequences in case of failure to comply as would have been the case if orders had been disobeyed by the Chief of the Main Staff. However, his attitude caused a lot of respect and fear with his inferiors or his subordinates. Not with all of them, mind you, but that is certainly what most of them appear to have felt.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Particularly, if we bear in mind the influence that Mr. Vasiljevic had with the federal secretary?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that, at the time, Mr. Vasiljevic held under control the entire security structure of the then-JNA? And that no action or operation of any consequence within the security and counter-intelligence sector could have been carried out without his knowledge and explicit approval?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, can you please be more specific about the time?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. 1990 and 1991. From March onwards, I can't say. In 1991, up until March, I know that he enjoyed no absolute authority with me. I was independent in making assessments, and I would act based on my own assessments. There were other individuals, later on, who were anxious about holding down their positions and thought the best idea was to obey him, although they sometimes disagreed. Specifically, I know some examples from the land forces at the time. From the air force, too, for that matter, but as time went by, in 1991, his authority and his influence grew and continued to grow.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Following the arrival of Mr. Vasiljevic at the head of the security administration, did the scope of activities of the security organs start to include the civilian sector, which up to then had not been within their remit?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Were three new groups not created at the time in order to monitor society outside the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the air force, that is correct. Three new detachments were set up, one in Zagreb, one in Sarajevo, and one in Nis. These detachments were supposed, as of sometime around 1988 or 1989, to deal with the society, which up until then had not been the case and had even been forbidden by the rules of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the Zagreb-based detachment? Were they given the task to deal with the Croatian political leadership and members of the MUP and to set up a network of associates in those structures?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did this happen after the multi-party elections in Croatia also?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It grew in intensity after the multi-party elections but also on the eve of the elections, when the first political parties were created in late 1989. That's when they set about doing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about this network of associates? Did they not try to recruit people among the very leaders of Croatia's political life?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the nature of the service to get as close to the top as possible, to have the top-most source possible, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was there a plan for this network of associates to continue to exist once the JNA left Croatian territory?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're talking about the 2nd Detachment, then I would say that's true. That was the objective. That was the task. Leave strongholds behind in the territory even once the JNA had withdrawn from the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The next step was to expand this network of associates to the media; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that was the first step. That was the step that was taken first. And then the move was made to the party political leadership because at the time, and we all were witnesses of that, the media had a very important role in creating public opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: This operation that we are talking about conducted by the 2nd Detachment did it remain secret until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It remained secret until the barracks was captured where they had their headquarters. Then the Croatian security services analysed the seized materials quite soon after that, but I can't tell you exactly how -- after how much time they analysed these materials. But this operation did not remain a secret right until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You talked about going into the barracks where these materials were seized. When was this?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in 1991, in the Maksimirska barracks, where they had their headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, the date actually was the 15th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: We will come back to this a bit later. In the conversations you mentioned here that you had with General Raseta, did the JNA make an offer for Vukovar to be an open city, without access allowed to any army?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall Raseta ever offering such an option. There is a very objective record of what Raseta offered and also what my response was in the minutes made by the ECMM observers. I think that that is the most objective record of what was offered, who offered what, and what the response was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because you said that you spent every day sitting at the table and conducted negotiations conducive to resolving problem situations.

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day, from the 8th of October, almost until the end of 1991, yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know that until November 1991 the road between Vukovar and Vinkovci, via Luci [phoen], Bogdanovci, Marinci, Nustar, was open?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know that it was open until that time. Specifically, it was my task to visit Vukovar on the 30th of September, 1991, and I was not able to enter. I came to Bogdanovci, to the defence command. I was in contact with the commander of the Vukovar defence. And it was not possible for me to get into Vukovar because it was besieged entirely, and this access road from Bogdanovci was under the control of the JNA or the TO. In any case, the first convoy that we organised to bring out the wounded was at that time because already at that time it was not possible freely to enter Vukovar. So that was that period, between the 8th and the 12th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned the convoy, didn't the convoy actually enter in that way to Vukovar, under the escort of the ZNG, and it happened without the knowledge and escort of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IMRA AGOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not the case at all. It arrived escorted by doctors from Doctors Without Borders. The vehicles used were civilian vehicles that went there. At no time did the ZNG members move beyond the line of separation between the Croatian forces and the other side. It is true that members of the ZNG were able to enter Vukovar at the time. Had that been possible, then the wounded would have been brought out in a day or two. A convoy is a complicated thing and you need four or five days in order to do that. I have it written down somewhere. It was stopped, it was searched by members of the JNA. Specifically I remember a Lieutenant Colonel Milenkovic, this has stuck to my mind, who kept searching over and over, each of the vehicles, the ambulances. He made threats and so on. I remember that surname of that specific JNA member.
